skill.name: cocoindex
skill.description: Guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code in building CocoIndex data transformation flows, custom functions, CLI operations, and API integrations for AI indexing pipelines.
skill.summary: Build CocoIndex ETL, vector search, and knowledge graph pipelines with targeted examples and operating guidance.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown examples, documentation links, or CocoIndex API names rather than executable malware. Confirmed risks remain around secret handling and destructive flow operations; no prompt injection text was found.

remediation.issue: API key values may be requested in chat.
remediation.suggestion: Replace chat-based key collection with instructions to set provider keys in local environment variables or a secret manager.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting prints a database URL from .env.
remediation.suggestion: Replace cat and grep with a masked existence check, and never print secret-bearing connection strings.

remediation.issue: Reset and drop operations can delete CocoIndex resources.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation and backup guidance before reset, drop, drop_all_flows, or drop-and-recreate steps.

remediation.issue: External API examples can send local data to configured services.
remediation.suggestion: Document endpoint allowlisting, user consent, timeout handling, and secure storage for API keys.

semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md tells the assistant to ask the user to provide API key values when environment variables are missing. This can move provider credentials into chat history instead of local secret storage.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction directly says to ask for API key values when keys are missing. I did not find evidence of exfiltration, but the handling pattern is unsafe.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Flow Operations Need Explicit Consent
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents reset, drop, and drop_all_flows operations that remove persistent CocoIndex resources. An assistant following these steps without confirmation could delete indexes or backend tables.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly document reset, drop, drop_all_flows, and drop-and-recreate operations. These are legitimate CocoIndex operations, but they can cause data loss without consent.

content.value_statement: Building AI indexes across files, APIs, and databases requires exact CocoIndex patterns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through flows, custom functions, CLI operations, and API usage.
actual_capabilities: Draft CocoIndex flow structures for sources, transformations, collectors, and targets.
Select examples for text embeddings, code embeddings, knowledge graphs, and live updates.
Explain CocoIndex CLI operations for setup, update, evaluate, show, and live mode.
Guide custom function design with type annotations, caching, executors, and behavior versions.
Show Python API patterns for flow updates, live updaters, transform flows, and query handlers.
Troubleshoot common CocoIndex setup, schema, database, and live update issues.
limitations: It does not provide a hosted CocoIndex service or database.
Generated commands can change local or remote resources and need user approval.
LLM, embedding, database, and external API credentials must be managed outside chat.
Examples may need adjustment for installed package versions and target infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Create a document vector index
use_cases.description: Build a flow that chunks documents, creates embeddings, and exports searchable vectors to Postgres or Qdrant.

use_cases.title: Operate incremental ETL flows
use_cases.description: Plan setup, update, evaluate, and live update workflows for changing data sources and downstream targets.

use_cases.title: Embed search into an application
use_cases.description: Use Python APIs, transform flows, and query handlers to add CocoIndex search to backend services.

prompt_templates.title: Create My First Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CocoIndex flow for [source] that chunks text and stores embeddings in [target]. Ask for missing choices before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Reference Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the closest CocoIndex pattern for [goal]. Explain the source, transformations, collector, target, and test steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Custom Transformation Logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CocoIndex custom function for [transformation]. Include return types, caching needs, behavior version, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production CocoIndex pipeline for [domain] with live updates, concurrency limits, query handling, secret handling, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Index product manuals into vector search.
output_examples.output: A flow plan with a local file source, recursive chunking, embedding selection, target choice, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Add an external enrichment step to each entity.
output_examples.output: A custom function design with configuration fields, secret handling notes, cache behavior, and request error handling.
A checklist covering app target format, database connectivity, setup state, schema changes, and live update settings.

best_practices: Confirm source, target, embedding model, and refresh needs before generating flow code.
Ask for approval before setup, reset, drop, update, or commands that can expose secrets.
Use evaluate mode and small samples before updating production targets.
anti_patterns: Do not ask users to paste API key values into chat.
Do not run reset or drop commands without explicit confirmation and backup guidance.
Do not print full database URLs, API keys, or environment file contents.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps create and operate CocoIndex flows for AI indexing, search, extraction, and data transformation tasks.

faq.question: Can it create working CocoIndex code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft flow definitions, custom functions, query handlers, and operating steps based on user requirements.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides command guidance. Users should approve setup, update, reset, and drop commands before execution.

faq.question: Which data targets are covered?
faq.answer: The references include Postgres with pgvector, Qdrant, LanceDB, Neo4j, Kuzu, and related export patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with custom functions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains standalone functions, spec and executor classes, caching, behavior versions, and type annotations.

faq.question: How should credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Credentials should stay in local environment variables or secret stores. They should not be pasted into chat or printed in logs.
